_comment: TM definitions (R4.4, GAME_DESIGN.md 13). A TM is found once in the world; picking it up puts a matching `kind: "tm"` ITEM in the satchel (OF29 -- the id here and the item id in data/items/items.json are deliberately the same string, which is the only link between the two files), and teaching spends that item. `move_id` must exist in data/moves/moves.json; `compatible_types` lists which data/creatures/species.json `type` values may learn it. Same-type only for this pass -- 13's 'off-type moves are allowed when physically/thematically sensible' is a real design call this data does not make on its own.
_comment_consumed: OF29 supersedes R4.4's reading of GAME_DESIGN.md 13's 'not consumed after one teaching'. The owner asked to 'choose who to teach it to', which only means anything if a copy teaches ONE creature -- so a TM item is consumed on teach and a second creature needs a second copy. Reverting to the never-consumed reading is one line: drop the `inventory.remove()` call in scripts/ui/tab_backpack.gd::_on_target_row()'s TM branch.
_comment_catalogue: Owner, after playing: there were exactly TWO TMs in the game, both ground, and each taught a move some creature already had -- "far too few" and "they're not upgrades". Both halves needed the move work that landed alongside this: while every move was power 1.0 with the same reach and timing, there was nothing for an upgrade to BE better than. TM moves now sit at 1.15x-2.0x a base move's power and buy real reach or area with it, and the 2.0x tier (earthshatter, leviathan_surge, heavenfall) is deliberately one per type and deliberately rare. Compatibility stays same-type-only; GAME_DESIGN.md 13's 'off-type moves where thematically sensible' is still a design call nobody has made, and this data does not make it.
